options: A major server function, like AD DS, DNS, or DHCP, added through Server Manager or Install-WindowsFeature
A user account with administrator rights
A smaller supporting capability a role might need, like .NET Framework
A type of Group Policy Object
questions.explain: A role is a major function such as Active Directory Domain Services, DNS Server, or DHCP Server. A feature is a smaller supporting capability a role might need.

questions.q: Why is the DNS Server role almost always installed alongside AD DS?
options: AD DS depends on DNS for workstations to locate a domain controller in the first place
DNS is required to issue Kerberos tickets
DNS and AD DS are actually the same role with two names
It isn't related — they're installed together purely by convention
questions.explain: AD DS cannot function without DNS, since name resolution is how a workstation finds a domain controller to authenticate against.

questions.q: What does SYSVOL store on a domain controller?
options: Group Policy Objects and domain logon scripts
The Kerberos ticket cache for logged-in users
DHCP lease assignments
The IIS website files for the domain
questions.explain: SYSVOL is the shared folder on every DC holding Group Policy Objects and logon scripts, which workstations read when policy is applied.

questions.q: What happens when a user logs into a domain-joined computer?
options: The computer sends the credentials to a domain controller, which verifies them and issues a Kerberos ticket
The computer checks the password against a local file and never contacts the network
The DHCP server verifies the password
IIS verifies the password through a web form
questions.explain: The domain controller checks the credentials against its copy of the AD database and, if they match, issues a Kerberos ticket proving the user's identity to other servers.

questions.q: What is replication, in the context of multiple domain controllers?
options: The automatic process by which DCs keep their copies of the AD database in sync with each other
The process of copying files to a File Server share
A backup job that runs once per week
The process of installing the same role on every server
questions.explain: Each DC keeps its own full copy of the AD database (ntds.dit) and automatically replicates changes to the others, so a change made on one DC propagates domain-wide.
